brief: Seventeen plots, a harvest cycle, a cart and a glasshouse — and not one tool. The allotments are the most worked ground in the town and carry no shed, no water butt, no bean canes, no cloche, no compost bay, no barrow: a plot is a rectangle of soil with a crop drawn on it. Give the plots their furniture on ROOF_FURN's model — a small set of pieces placed per plot off hash(plot), each one inside its own plot's rectangle (the lattice is ox 80..90 step 5 x oy 8..50 step 7, which leaves a 1-cell way round every plot), and each one named by the pointer the way roofFurnAt names the roof's. Let the set read the plot's own state: canes where something climbs, a cloche in the cold half of the year, a barrow only where somebody is working it, a butt against the fence.
seams: the plot lattice (the ox/oy loops near lines 3486 and 3510)
successLooksLike: At the Street quarter the allotments read as seventeen worked plots rather than seventeen coloured rectangles; every piece sits inside its own plot and clear of the ways; the pointer names each kind; and `structures` moves (a new named array in __census()'s structure block), baseline re-pinned and said so.
avoid: Nothing on the 1-cell ways between plots and nothing inside the glasshouse footprint. Do not add a tile kind or a SPECIES — each moves tileKinds/speciesKinds by exactly 9 and that is not what this is measuring. Do not draw it live: the plots are ground-cache work.
